key_insight: A mean-flow-based ROM can explicitly model nonlinear Reynolds-stress effects and produce turbulence statistics close to DNS in channel flow.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more accurate reduced-order surrogate for wall-bounded turbulence, with potential for faster analysis and forecasting in CFD workflows.
method: Build Galerkin ROMs from linearized Navier–Stokes modes around the mean flow.
Modify the modal basis so Reynolds-stress divergence is represented consistently in the reduced equations.
Compare balanced truncation and controllability modes against POD for short-time prediction and reconstruction.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports DNS-level statistical agreement in a minimal channel at Re_tau ≈ 185 and shows balanced truncation modes outperform controllability modes in short-time forecasting.
watch_item: The framework depends on accurate mean-flow information and reduced-basis choices, so performance may degrade when extending to higher Reynolds numbers or less resolved flows.
paper_title: Mean-flow-based reduced-order models of turbulent channel flow
